dedupe_keys.name: accessx open source python library for urban accessibility and equity analysis

description: accessX is an open-source Python library from Transform Transport, introduced on its site in July 2026, that provides an end-to-end, modular workflow for urban accessibility analysis, from spatial data acquisition and preprocessing to accessibility and equity evaluation. Coverage: it uses OpenStreetMap, WorldPop and user-provided datasets, supports flexible travel-cost assumptions, isochrone generation and established accessibility measures, and its application to Amsterdam, Athens and Milan shows consistent, transparent assessments of pedestrian accessibility and equity. The authors argue that accessibility studies are often built from fragmented scripts, datasets and case-specific assumptions, which makes results hard to reproduce or compare, a concern they see as sharper with AI-assisted analysis. Format and access: a Python library described in an article on the Transform Transport site. Licence and cost: free and open source; the licence was not stated on the page read. Caveats: the examples are pedestrian accessibility in three cities. The workflow can prepare walking network and opportunity inputs for accessibility-based capacity planning and network flow studies. It relates to OpenStreetMap and the HeiGIT accessibility indicators in the catalogue.
